title: Nucleic acid detection with CRISPR-Cas13a/C2c2
status: Peer-reviewed Science article; PMC author manuscript
summary: Collateral cleavage becomes a programmable diagnostic readout.

conceptual.rationale: Integrates existing sensing and amplification principles.

observability.rationale: Sensitive DNA/RNA detection and allele discrimination.

controls.rationale: Matched targets and established assay comparisons.

statistics.rationale: Small technical-replicate sets limit population inference.

scope.rationale: Clinical promise exceeds demonstrated diagnostic validation.

reproducibility.rationale: Methods supplement located but not read.

depth.rationale: Amplification and specimen provenance change interpretation.

novelty.comparator: East-Seletsky et al. 2016, RNA detection with C2c2
novelty.increment: Amplification-coupled sensitivity plus diverse diagnostic demonstrations.
novelty.limit: Collateral-RNA detection predates SHERLOCK; priority search is incomplete.

details.observation: Cas13a alone reaches approximately 50 fM; amplification enables attomolar detection.
details.interpretation: Sensitivity belongs to the coupled workflow.
details.boundary: This is not amplification-free single-molecule detection.

details.observation: Cancer-mutation experiments use mock cell-free DNA.
details.interpretation: Low allele fractions are an analytical demonstration.
details.boundary: They do not establish patient-level cancer diagnostic accuracy.

nextTest: Blind a prospective specimen panel with prespecified thresholds, extraction procedures and clinical sensitivity/specificity.

read: Main text and all figure captions through NCBI BioC XML
notRead: Separate supplementary methods PDF: download returned HTML

title: Drag-and-drop genome insertion of large sequences without double-strand DNA cleavage using CRISPR-directed integrases
status: Peer-reviewed Nature Biotechnology article; PMC author manuscript
summary: Prime-editing landing sites recruit integrases for large-cargo insertion.

conceptual.rationale: Substantial synthesis of prime editing and integration.
conceptual.locator: Introduction; Results, PASTE combines CRISPR editing

observability.rationale: Large-cargo insertion across several biological settings.

diversity.rationale: Sequencing, expression, primary-cell and animal evidence.

statistics.rationale: Replicate and sampling units require careful interpretation.

scope.rationale: Primary-hepatocyte efficiency uses sorted transfected cells.
scope.locator: Results, PASTE efficiency in non-dividing and primary cells

reproducibility.rationale: Detailed methods, deposited reads, plasmids and code.

depth.rationale: Nicking and sample denominators reshape headline claims.

novelty.comparator: Anzalone et al., twinPE plus Bxb1 (online 2021; issue 2022)
novelty.increment: Optimized fusion/recruitment, larger tested cargo and expanded delivery settings.
novelty.limit: Prime-editing-enabled integrase insertion already existed; not global priority certification.

details.observation: PASTE employs Cas9 nickase and flap repair.
details.interpretation: It avoids reliance on exposed double-strand-break repair.
details.boundary: It does not eliminate DNA nicking or all cellular repair.
details.locator: Results, PASTE combines CRISPR editing; Fig. 1A–D

details.observation: Fig. 6F points represent different liver regions.
details.interpretation: Spatial samples are not automatically independent animals.
details.boundary: Do not interpret the stated n=8 as eight independent mice.
details.locator: Fig. 6F caption; Methods, In vivo injections of PASTE adenovirus

nextTest: Replicate across donors using prespecified unsorted-cell denominators and long-read on/off-target integration assessment.

read: Main results; selected quantification, off-target, modelling and animal methods
All main figure captions; data availability; comparator primary record
notRead: Raw reads, code execution or plasmid verification

title: Programmable RNA-guided DNA endonucleases are widespread in eukaryotes and their viruses
summary: Genome mining connects diverse Fanzors to programmable nuclease activity.

conceptual.rationale: Broad evolutionary organization beyond earlier Fanzor characterization.

diversity.rationale: Sequence, RNA, biochemical and cellular convergence.

statistics.rationale: Quantified screens; selected enzymes constrain generalization.

scope.rationale: Native transposon function remains explicitly unresolved.

reproducibility.rationale: Detailed methods and named data/material resources.
reproducibility.locator: Methods; Data and materials availability: PRJNA1002369

depth.rationale: Inactive examples bound the computational catalogue.

novelty.comparator: Saito et al. 2023, Fanzor is a eukaryotic programmable RNA-guided endonuclease
novelty.increment: Broader census, evolutionary analysis and additional biochemical/cellular characterization.
novelty.limit: June 2023 comparator already demonstrated Fanzor programmability; endogenous function remains unresolved.

details.observation: 3,655 clustered candidates are mined; only selected enzymes are tested.
details.interpretation: Catalogue breadth is not equivalent to validated enzyme breadth.
details.boundary: Activity cannot be assigned to every candidate.

details.observation: CrFNuc-1 forms an RNA complex but shows no detected cleavage.
details.interpretation: RNA association alone does not establish nuclease activity.
details.boundary: Failed reconstitution and native inactivity remain alternatives.
details.locator: Results, fRNA-guided DNA endonucleases are present in diverse eukaryotic genomes, final paragraph

nextTest: Test native-host Fanzor loss and rescue for transposon persistence, separating nuclease activity from association.

read: Main text, figures, computational discovery/phylogeny, biochemical and mammalian-editing methods via BioC
PMC data/material statement; comparator primary PubMed record
notRead: Raw sequencing, deposited plasmids and native-host functional experiments
